A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dejavu/EFN research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison; the missing CALVIN material in v3 is an actual removal.

before.justification: v2 reports original EFN experiments on LIBERO, CALVIN and real-world AgiBot-G1 tasks, together with ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original LIBERO and AgiBot-G1 experiments, ablations, memory-bank analyses and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The frozen VLA backbone, retrieval-conditioned residual architecture, similarity-shaped SAC training, anti-idling reward and successful-rollout memory growth remain unchanged. The revised descriptions do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v3 removes CALVIN entirely, including its 34-task, chained-language-goal evaluation in held-out environment D. This substantially narrows coverage of compositional and cross-environment generalization. The four LIBERO suites and four AgiBot-G1 tasks remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same frozen backbones and kNN-RAG, ResAct, R2A and GC-TTT baselines, with unchanged adapted implementations in Appendix B.4. The deleted CALVIN experiment used this same comparator set; its removal changes coverage rather than comparator membership.

E3.justification: The distinct CALVIN protocol disappears: training on A/B/C, testing on D using 1,000 five-goal chains, reporting Success@1–5 and average completed chain length, and evaluating banks of 2,000 and 5,000. Retained LIBERO and robot settings are unchanged; this is protocol removal, not evidence of rerunning existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 10(b)'s CALVIN bank-capacity sensitivity analysis is removed. The corresponding LIBERO and robot curves remain in v3 Figure C.1, alongside unchanged component ablations, bank-composition and update-rule analyses, runtime studies and the direct-action negative result.

E5.justification: Both versions retain averaging over three seeds and the same 50-episode-per-task-per-seed disclosure in Appendix B.4. No new uncertainty-reporting practice, significance test or repeated-run procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: The entire CALVIN result table and capacity curves are removed. For example, v2 Table 5 reports OpenVLA Success@5 of 0.430 versus 0.508 with EFN at volume 5,000; neither entry remains in v3. Numerical values in all corresponding retained benchmark, ablation and runtime tables are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations for retrieval, rewards, SAC and residual control are retained. Appendix equations receive section-based numbering, but no substantive derivation, assumption, theorem or proof changes.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims, with a 'to our knowledge' qualification, that EFN is the first frozen-VLA post-deployment framework combining live experience accumulation with retrieval-conditioned residual correction. This priority claim is absent from v2; the central method and performance claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: Removing v2 Appendix E.1 also removes its explanation that CALVIN results demonstrate transfer without nearly identical scenes or test-environment memories, through semantic transition similarity. The broader mechanism discussion and limitations concerning backbone quality, cold starts and bank growth remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces v2's statement that code and demos are in supplementary material with a project-page link. Retained architecture, storage, hyperparameter and runtime-measurement details are essentially unchanged. The PDFs establish the changed access information, not the linked resources' availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for Sinkhorn distances, Adam, retrieval-augmented generation and Residual Policy Learning, removes the CALVIN reference, and introduces explicit 'first framework' positioning. Other reference edits largely update metadata or consolidate duplicate entries rather than change the cited research.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and appendix prose receive sentence-level editing, with added acknowledgments and corresponding-author markers. Appendix numbering and cross-references are revised. The narrative and section hierarchy remain largely intact apart from the CALVIN subsection's removal.

P2.justification: v2 Table 5 is deleted, and the three-panel Figure 10 becomes two larger panels in v3 Figure C.1 after removing CALVIN. Diagram labels, captions and appendix display numbering are edited, with local reflow; the remaining figures, table structures and overall layout are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides editorial polish, additional foundational citations and clearer resource-access information, but removes CALVIN ABC→D evidence addressing whether retrieval remains useful in unseen environments without matching scene memories. This meaningfully weakens support for generalization, without replacement evidence. The unchanged method and substantial retained LIBERO and robot evaluations limit the deterioration.
